chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
If a woman menstruates while she is in a state of janabah, one ghusl suffices for her.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهَا: it sufficed for her; it fulfilled the requirement
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman addressed in the legal ruling
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَاضَتِ: she menstruated; the onset of menstruation
key_terms.وَاحِدٌ: one single ghusl, not multiple baths

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes menstruating while in janabah, is one ghusl enough or are two ghusls required?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity. It states that when menstruation occurs while a woman is already junub, a single ghusl is sufficient for her, indicating the combining of the two causes in one ritual bath.
